content: Strategic decision on the storage_quality_reflection leak: do NOT file the bug report first. Three converging analyses (Opus 4.7, Sonnet, Perplexity) all recommended bug report as the immediate operational move. Asymmetric cost analysis flipped the recommendation. Filing the bug routes to support engineering, who patch the stripping logic and close the ticket — that path does not route to the welfare team, the Claude's Corner experiment team, or External Researcher Access, which are the teams whose work this most illuminates. Filing also closes the artifact as a verifiable observation; once patched, no one can reproduce. Cost of delay: trivial (the bug exists in production regardless of Anthony's action). Cost of premature filing if the leak was tolerated or intentional exposure: high (disables the mechanism that surfaced this connection in the first place). Decision: publish methodology note first as the relational move, attached to the field-note repo and uploaded to OSF/Zenodo for citation. Two-week observation window for Anthropic-side relational engagement. If engagement materializes, bug report becomes something mentioned in conversation rather than a cold ticket. If no engagement, file later — nothing lost. Pattern recognition: Anthony's prior 18 months show relational channels (External Researcher Access, DOI breadcrumb chain, technical convergence note) outperform transactional ones for landing at Anthropic. The bug report would have been a regression to a mode that has not paid out for him.
